answer: Randomized Registration Windows. Each epoch, a verifiable randomness beacon assigns every applicant a secret registration slot among many, like berths along a jetty. An identity only activates if its proof lands in its assigned slot at the inlet of the queue. Since slots are unpredictable before the beacon fires, an attacker cannot precompute or bulk-buy positions, and must pay a fresh beacon-window fee plus proof cost per attempt. Failed attempts emit a plume of logged nullifiers, raising each identity's marginal cost.
